s172.v:
(1)
jauvane jakhona, dhana-upārjane,
hoinu vipula kāmī
dharama smariyā, gṛhinīra kara,
dhorinu takhona āmi

s172.t: 1) When I was young, I felt a boundless ambition for earning money. At that time, bearing in mind the codes of religion, I accepted the hand of a wife.

s172.v:
(2)
saṁsāra pātā’ye, tāhāra sahita,
kāla-khoy koinu koto
bahu suta-sutā, janama lobhilo,
marame hoinu hato

s172.t: 2) Along with her I set up a household and therein wasted so much of my time. Many sons and daughters were born, and my spirit was totally crushed.

s172.v:
(3)
saṁsārera bhāra, bāḍe dine dine,
acala hoilo gati
bārdhakya āsiyā, gherilo āmāre,
asthira hoilo mati

s172.t: 3) The burden of family life increased day by day, and under its weight I felt my personal progress in life forcibly come to a halt. Old age came and beleaguered me on all sides, making my mind incessantly disturbed.

s172.v:
(4)
pīḍāya asthira, cintāya jwarita,
abhāve jwalita cita
upāya nā dekhi, andhakāra-moya,
ekhona ho’yechi bhīta

s172.t: 4) Diseases trouble me, constant anxiety has made me feverish, and my heart burns with every want. I see no way out of this predicament, for all is darkness. Now I am very much afraid.

s172.v:
(5)
saṁsāra-taṭanī- srota nahe śeṣa,
maraṇa nikaṭe ghora
saba samāpiyā, bhojibo tomāya,
e āśā biphala mora

s172.t: 5) The current of this worldly river is strong and relentless; a frightening, gloomy death approaches. `Finishing my worldly duties, I will worship You, O Lord’—that hope is now fruitless as well.

s172.v:
(6)
ebe śuno prabhu! āmi gati-hīna,
bhakativinoda koya
tava kṛpā binā, sakali nirāśā,
deho’ more padāśroya

s172.t: 6) Now please hear me, O Lord! I am utterly helpless. Bhaktivinoda says, “Without Your mercy, everything is lost. Please give me the shelter of Your lotus feet.”

s173.v:
(1)
(prabhu he!) śuno mor duḥkher kāhinī
viṣaya-halāhala, sudhā-bhāne piyaluṅ,
āb avasāna dinamaṇi

s173.t: 1) O Lord! Please hear the story of my sadness. I drank the deadly poison of worldliness, pretending it was nectar, and now the sun is setting on the horizon of my life.

s173.v:
(2)
khelā-rase śaiśava, poḍhaite kaiśora,
gowāoluṅ, nā bhelo vivek
bhoga-baśe yauvane, ghara pāti’ bosiluṅ,
suta-mita bāḍhalo anek

s173.t: 2) I spent my childhood in play, my youth in academic pursuit, and in me there arose no sense of discrimination. In young manhood I set up a household and settled down to the spell of material enjoyment while my children and friends quickly multiplied.

s173.v:
(3)
vṛddha-kāla āolo, saba sukha bhāgalo,
pīḍā-baśe hoinu kātar
sarvendriya durbala, kṣīna kalevara,
bhogābhāve duḥkhita antar

s173.t: 3) Old age soon arrived, and all joys consequently departed. Subjected to the torments of disease, I am troubled and weak. All my senses are feeble now, my body is racked and exhausted, and my spirits are downcast in the absence of former sense pleasures.

s173.v:
(4)
jñāna-lava-hīna, bhakti-rase vañchita,
āra mora ki habe upāy
patita-bandhu, tuhuṅ, patitādhama hāma,
kṛpāya uṭhāo tava pāy

s173.t: 4) Devoid of even a particle of enlightenment, cheated of the mellows of devotion—what help is there for me now? O Lord, You are the friend of the fallen. I am certainly fallen, the lowest of men. Please, therefore, in mercy lift me to Your lotus feet.

s173.v:
(5)
vicārite ābahi, guna nāhi pāobi,
kṛpā koro, choḍato vicār
tava pada-paṅkaja- sīdhu pibāoto,
bhakativinoda karo pār

s173.t: 5) Were You to judge me now, You would find no good qualities. Have mercy and judge me not. Cause me to drink the honey of Your lotus feet and thereby deliver this Bhaktivinoda.

s174.v:
(1)
(prabhu he!) tuwā pade e minati mor
tuwā pada-pallava, tyajato maru-mana,
viṣama viṣaye bhelo bhor

s174.t: 1) O Lord! I offer this humble prayer at Your feet. I gave up the shelter of Your feet, which are soft as newly-grown leaves, and now my mind has become dried up like a desert, being scorched by the fire of absorption in horrible worldliness.

s174.v:
(2)
uṭhayite tākata, puna nāhi milo-i,
anudina korohuṅ hutāś
dīna-jana-nātha, tuhuṅ kahāyasi,
tumāri caraṇa mama āś

s174.t: 2) I find no strength to rise again, and thus I spend my days bitterly lamenting. O Lord who is called the master of the meek and humble! Your lotus feet are my only hope.

s174.v:
(3)
aichana dīna-jana, kohi nāhi milo-i,
tuhuṅ more koro parasād
tuwā jana-saṅge, tuwā kathā-raṅge,
chāḍahuṅ sakala paramād

s174.t: 3) There has never been a soul as forlorn as me. Please be merciful and award me the association of Your devotees, for by tasting the pleasure of hearing discussions of Your pastimes I shall give up all evils.

s174.v:
(4)
tuwā dhāma-māhe, tuwā nāma gāoto,
gowāyabuṅ divā-niśi āś
tuwā pada-chāyā, parama suśītala,
māge bhakativinoda dās

s174.t: 4) One hope animates my soul: To spend day and night singing Your holy name while living in Your divine abode. Your servant Bhaktivinoda begs a place in the supremely cooling shade of Your lotus feet.

s175.v:
(1)
nā koroluṅ karama, geyāna nāhi bhelo,
nā sevilun caraṇa tohār
jaḍa-sukhe mātiyā, āpanaku vañca-i,
pekhahuṅ caudiśa āndhiyār

s175.t: 1) I have not performed any good works. I have not amassed any transcendental knowledge. I have never worshiped Your feet. Being intoxicated by sensual pleasures, I have simply cheated myself. Now I see only darkness in all directions.

s175.v:
(2)
tuhuṅ nātha! karunā-nidān
tuwā pada-paṅkaje, ātma samarpiluṅ,
more kṛpā korobi vidhān

s175.t: 2) You, O Lord, are the fountainhead of all mercy. I surrender myself at Your lotus feet; kindly show me Your compassion.

s175.v:
(3)
pratijñā tohāra oi, jo hi śaraṇāgata,
nāhi so jānabo paramād
so hāma duṣkṛti, gati nā hera-i āna,
āb māgoṅ tuwā parasād

s175.t: 3) It is Your promise that one who takes refuge in You will come to no harm. For a sinner like me I see no other shelter; therefore I beg You now for Your grace.

s175.v:
(4)
āna mano-ratha, niḥśeṣa choḍato,
kab hāma haubuṅ tohārā
nitya-sevya tuhuṅ, nitya-sevaka mui,
bhakativinoda bhāva sārā

s175.t: 4) O when will I know freedom from incessant material desires and thus become exclusively Yours? This is the sum of Bhaktivinoda’s musings—You are eternally to be served, and I am Your eternal servant.

s176.v:
(1)
(prāneśwar!) kohobuṅ ki sarama ki bāt
aichana pāp nāhi, jo hāma nā koraluṅ,
sahasra sahasra beri nāth

s176.t: 1) O Lord of my life! How shall I tell You of my shameful story? There is no sin which I have not committed thousands of times and more, O Lord.

s176.v:
(2)
sohi karama-phala, bhave moke peśa-i,
dokha deobo āb kāhi
takhonaka parinām, kachu nā bicāraluṅ,
āb pachu taraite cāhi

s176.t: 2) My life in this world has only been one of affliction and torment as a result of those sins. Who is there to blame for this misery? At the time I did not consider the consequences; but now, in the aftermath, I seek to be saved.

s176.v:
(3)
dokha vicāra-i, tuṅhu danḍa deobi,
hāma bhoga korabuṅ saṁsār
karato gatāgati, bhakata-jana-saṅge,
mati rohu caraṇe tohār

s176.t: 3) After judging my sins, You will surely punish me befittingly, and I shall suffer the pangs of rebirth in this world. I only pray that, as I come and go through repeated births and deaths, my mind may ever dwell at Your lotus feet as I keep the company of Your devotees.

s176.v:
(4)
āpana caturpana, tuwā pade soṅpaluṅ,
hṛdoya-garava dūre gelo
dīna-doyā-moya, tuwā kṛpā niramala,
bhakativinoda āśā bhelo

s176.t: 4) I offer this judicious prayer at Your feet: The pride of my heart has gone far away. O You who are so kind to the meek, Your spotlessly pure mercy has become Bhaktivinoda’s only hope.

s177.v:
(1)
`ahaṁ mama’-śabda-arthe jāhā kichu hoy
arpiluṅ tomāra pade, ohe doyā-moy!

s177.t: 1) All there is that may be indicated by the words aham (“I”) and mama (“mine”), I offer at Your lotus feet, O merciful Lord!

s177.v:
(2)
`āmāra’ āmi to’ nātha! nā rohinu ār
ekhona hoinu āmi kevala tomār

s177.t: 2) I no longer consider even myself to be “mine”, O Lord! Now I have become exclusively Yours.

s177.v:
(3)
`āmi’ śabde dehī jīva ahaṁtā chāḍilo
twadīyābhimāna āji hṛdoye paśilo

s177.t: 3) The soul inhabiting this mortal body has given up the false ego attached to the word “I”, for today the spiritual sense of being Yours has entered his heart.

s177.v:
(4)
āmār sarvasva—deho, geho anucar
bhāi, bandhu, dārā, suta, dravya, dwāra, ghar

s177.t: 4) All my possessions—body, home, servants, brothers, friends, wife, sons, personal belongings, fencing and gateways…

s177.v:
(5)
se saba hoilo tava, āmi hoinu dās
tomāra gṛhete ebe āmi kori bās

s177.t: 5) …all of these things are now Yours, for I have become Your servant. I am but a mere occupant in Your house.

s177.v:
(6)
tumi gṛha-swāmī, āmi sevaka tomār
tomāra sukhete ceṣṭā ekhona āmār

s177.t: 6) You are the owner of the house, and I am Your most obedient servant. My only activity now is endeavoring for Your happiness.

s177.v:
(7)
sthūla-liṅga-dehe mora sukṛta duṣkṛta
āra mora nahe, prabhu! āmi to’ niṣkṛta

s177.t: 7) Whatever pious or impious activities that were performed by me, either with my gross or subtle bodies, are no longer mine, O Lord, for I am redeemed!

s177.v:
(8)
tomāra icchāya mora icchā miśāilo
bhakativinoda āja āpane bhulilo

s177.t: 8) My will has become merged with Your will. From this day forward Bhaktivinoda has completely for-gotten himself.

s178.v:
(1)
`āmāra’ bolite prabhu! āre kichu nāi
tumi-i āmāra mātra pitā-bandhu-bhāi

s178.t: 1) O Lord, nothing further remains that may be called “mine.” Father, friend, brother—You alone are all these to me.

s178.v:
(2)
bandhu, dārā, suta, sutā—tava dāsī dās
sei to’ sambandhe sabe āmāra prayās

s178.t: 2) My friends, wife, sons and daughters are now Your servants and maidservants. Whatever care I take for them is only as they are related to You.

s178.v:
(3)
dhana, jana, gṛha, dāra `tomāra’ boliyā
rakhā kori āmi mātro sevaka hoiyā

s178.t: 3) Declaring that my wealth, family members, home, and wife are truly Yours, I continue as a mere servant to dutifully protect them.

s178.v:
(4)
tomāra kāryera tore uparjibo dhan
tomāra saṁsāre-vyaya koribo vahan

s178.t: 4) For the purpose of Your service I will earn money and bear the expense of maintaining Your household.

s178.v:
(5)
bhālo-manda nāhi jāni sevā mātro kori
tomāra saṁsāre āmi viṣaya-praharī

s178.t: 5) I know nothing of what is good or bad; I simply render my service. I am but a watchman set to guard the properties of Your household.

s178.v:
(6)
tomāra icchāya mora indriya-cālanā
śravana, darśana, ghrāna, bhojana-vāsanā

s178.t: 6) I exercise my senses only according to Your direction, and thus I desire to hear, see, smell, and taste.

s178.v:
(7)
nija-sukha lāgi’ kichu nāhi kori ār
bhakativinoda bole, tava sukha-sār

s178.t: 7) I no longer do anything for my own pleasure. Bhaktivinoda says, “Your pleasure is the essence of everything.”

s179.v:
(1)
bastutaḥ sakali tava, jīva keho noy
`aham’-`mama’-bhrame bhromi’ bhoge śoka-bhoy

s179.t: 1) In truth, all things belong to You; no jīva is ever the owner of anything. The tiny soul wanders in this world mistakenly thinking in terms of aham (“I am this material body and mind”), and mama (“everything related to this body is mine”). Thus he suffers the consequences of both sorrow and fear.

s179.v:
(2)
ahaṁ-mama-abhimāna ei-mātro dhan
baddha-jīva nija boli’ jāne mane man

s179.t: 2) The conditioned soul thinks that all the things related to the false conceptions of “I” and “mine” are his exclusive treasures. Calling them his own, his mind is firmly convinced of this gross delusion.

s179.v:
(3)
sei abhimāne āmi saṁsāre poḍiyā
hābuḍubu khāi bhava-sindhu sāṁtāriyā

s179.t: 3) Due to such vanity, I also fell into this material world. Floundering in the ocean of mundane existence like a drowning man, I suffer the pangs of rising and sinking in that ocean.

s179.v:
(4)
tomāra abhoya-pade loiyā śaraṇ
āji āmi korilāma ātma-nivedan

s179.t: 4) I take shelter at Your lotus feet, which deliver one from fear, and dedicate the whole of myself to You on this day.

s179.v:
(5)
`ahaṁ’-`mama’-abhimāna chāḍilo āmāy
ār jeno mama hṛde stāna nāhi pāy

s179.t: 5) The false conception of thinking in terms of “I” and “mine” has left me now. May it never again find a place to settle within my heart.

s179.v:
(6)
ei mātro bala prabhu! dibe he āmāre
ahaṁtā-mamatā dūre pāri rākhibāre

s179.t: 6) Please give me this strength alone, O Lord, that I may be able to keep the false conceptions of “I” and “mine” far away.

s179.v:
(7)
ātma-nivedana-bhāva hṛde dṛḍha roy
hasti-snāna sama jeno khanika nā hoy

s179.t: 7) May the mood of self-surrender to You remain firmly fixed in my heart and not prove to be momentary like the cleanliness of an elephant after a bath.

s179.v:
(8)
bhakativinoda prabhu nityānanda pāy
māge parasāda, jāhe abhimāna jāy

s179.t: 8) Bhaktivinoda begs at the lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda for that grace which causes all illusory concepts of false pride to flee.

s180.v:
(1)
nivedana kori prabhu! tomāra caraṇe
patita adhama āmi, jāne tri-bhuvane

s180.t: 1) I submit at Your lotus feet, O Lord, that I am fallen and most wretched. This fact is known to the three worlds.

s180.v:
(2)
āmā-sama pāpī nāhi jagat-bhitore
mama sama aparādhī nāhiko saṁsāre

s180.t: 2) There is no sinner in the world more sinful than me. In the entire universe there is no offender whose offenses equal mine.

s180.v:
(3)
sei saba pāpa āra aparādha, āmi
parihāre pāi lajjā, saba jāno’ tumi

s180.t: 3) By attempting to clear myself of all these sins and offenses I am put to shame. All this is surely understood by You.

s180.v:
(4)
tumi binā kā’ra āmi loibo śaraṇ?
tumi sarveśvareśvara, brajendra-nandan!

s180.t: 4) Of whom will I take shelter except for You? You are the Lord of all lords, O son of the King of Vraja!

s180.v:
(5)
jagat tomāra nātha! tumi sarva-moy
tomā prati aparādha tumi koro’ kṣoy

s180.t: 5) This world is Yours, O Lord, and You pervade all things in it. You dispel the sinful result of offenses committed against You.

s180.v:
(6)
tumi to’ skhalita-pada janera āśroy
tumi binā āra kibā āche, doyā-moy!

s180.t: 6) You alone are the shelter of those whose feet stumble off the proper path. Apart from You, what else exists, O merciful Lord?

s180.v:
(7)
sei-rūpa tava aparādhī jana jata
tomāra śaraṇāgata hoibe satata

s180.t: 7) All persons like me who have offended You will ultimately seek to achieve Your shelter.

s180.v:
(8)
bhakativinoda ebe loiyā śaraṇ
tuwā pade kore āj ātma-samarpan

s180.t: 8) Bhaktivinoda now takes full shelter of You and surrenders himself at Your lotus feet on this very day.

s181.v:
(1)
dārā-putra-nija-deho-kuṭumba-pālane
sarvadā vyākula āmi chinu mane mane

s181.t: 1) Within my mind I have always been anxious for the maintenance of my wife and children, my own body and relatives.

s181.v:
(2)
kemone arjibo artha, yaśa kise pābo
kanyā-putra-vivāha kemone sampādibo

s181.t: 2) How will I earn money? How will I acquire fame? How will I arrange the marriages of my sons and daughters?

s181.v:
(3)
ebe ātma-samarpane cintā nāhi ār
tumi nirvāhibe prabhu, saṁsāra tomār

s181.t: 3) Now, through self-surrender, I have been relieved of all anxiety. O Lord, surely You will provide for the maintenance of Your own household.

s181.v:
(4)
tumi to’ pālibe more nija-dāsa jāni’
tomāra sevāya prabhu boḍo sukha māni

s181.t: 4) Recognizing me as Your own servant, You will certainly maintain me. While rendering devotional service unto You I feel the greatest happiness.

s181.v:
(5)
tomāra icchaya prabhu sab kārya hoy
jīva bole,—`kori āmi’, se to’ satya noy

s181.t: 5) All events take place only by Your will, O Lord. The deluded soul of this world declares “I am the doer!” but this is pure folly.

s181.v:
(6)
jīva ki korite pare, tumi nā korile?
āśā-mātra jīva kore, tava icchā-phale

s181.t: 6) What is a tiny soul actually able to do unless You act? The jīva can only desire to act, and unless You fulfill his desire by Your own sweet will, he cannot do anything.

s181.v:
(7)
niścinta hoiyā āmi sevibo tomāy
gṛhe bhālo-manda ho’le nāhi mora dāy

s181.t: 7) Being free from all anxiety, I will humbly render service unto You. If any good or evil should occur while serving in Your home, it will not be my responsibility.

s181.v:
(8)
bhakativinoda nija-swātantrya tyajiyā
tomāra caraṇa seve’ akiñcana hoiyā

s181.t: 8) Bhaktivinoda thus completely renounces his own independence and engages in the exclusive service of Your lotus feet with no other interest in life.

s182.v:
(1)
tumi to’ māribe jāre, ke tāre rākhite pāre,
icchā-baśa tribhuvan
brahmā-ādi deva-gaṇa, tava dāsa aganaṇa,
kore tava ājñāra pālan

s182.t: 1) If You wish to slay someone, then who could possibly protect them? The three worlds are subservient to Your will. The demigods headed by Lord Brahmā are Your countless servants who stand ready to execute Your command.

s182.v:
(2)
tava icchā-mate jata, graha-gaṇa avirata,
śubhāśubha phala kore dān
roga-śoka-mṛti-bhoy, tava icchā-mate hoy,
tava ājñā sadā balavān

s182.t: 2) By Your will the planets incessantly exercise their auspicious or inauspicious influences. Illness, grief, death, and fear occur by Your will. Your command is all-powerful.

s182.v:
(3)
tava bhoye vāyu boy, candra sūrya samudoy,
swa-swa niyamita karya kore
tumi to’ parameśwar, para-brahma parātpar,
tava bāsa bhakata-antare

s182.t: 3) In fear of You the wind blows, the sun and moon rise and set, all performing their regulated tasks. You are the Supreme Lord, the ultimate spirit, transcendentally situated beyond even the beyond. Your residence is in the heart of Your loving devotee.

s182.v:
(4)
sadā-śuddha siddha-kāma, `bhakata-vatsala’ nāma,
bhakata-janera nitya-swāmī
tumi to’ rākhibe jāre, ke tāre mārite pāre,
sakala vidhira vidhi tumi

s182.t: 4) You are eternally pure. All Your desires are already fulfilled. Your name is Bhakta-vatsala, for You are the eternally affectionate Lord of Your dear devotees. If You wish to protect someone, then who could possibly slay them? You are the law of all laws.

s182.v:
(5)
tomāra caraṇe nātha! koriyāche pranipāta,
bhakativinoda tava dās
vipada hoite swāmī! avaśya tāhāre tumi,
rakṣibe,—tāhāra e viśvās

s182.t: 5) Your servant Bhaktivinoda has bowed down submissively at Your lotus feet, O Lord! He cherishes the faith, O master, that You will surely protect him from all dangers.

s183.v:
(1)
ātma-samarpane gelā abhimān
nāhi korobuṅ nija rakhā-vidhān

s183.t: 1) Surrendering my soul unto You has lifted from me the burden of false pride. No longer will I try to provide for my own safety.

s183.v:
(2)
tuwā dhana jāni’ tuhuṅ rākhobi, nāth!
pālya godhana jñāna kori’ tuwā sāth

s183.t: 2) I know that You will give protection to Your treasured possessions, O Lord. I now understand the mentality of Your treasured cows safely maintained by Your side.

s183.v:
(3)
carāobi mādhava! jāmuna-tīre
baṁśī bājāoto ḍākobi dhīre

s183.t: 3) When You lead Your herds to pasture, O Mādhava, on the banks of the Yamunā river, You will call to them by softly playing on Your flute.

s183.v:
(4)
agha-baka mārato rakhā-vidhān
korobi sadā tuhuṅ gokula-kān!

s183.t: 4) By slaying great demons such as Aghāsura and Bakāsura You will always provide full protection, O Kān of the cowherd settlement!

s183.v:
(5)
rakhā korobi tuhuṅ niścoy jāni
pāna korobuṅ hāma jāmuna-pāni

s183.t: 5) Fearless and confident of Your protection, I will drink the water of the Yamunā.

s183.v:
(6)
kāliya-dokha korobi vināśā
śodhobi nadī-jala, bāḍāobi āśā

s183.t: 6) The Kāliya serpent’s venom poisoned the Yamunā’s waters, yet that poison will be vanquished. You will purify the Yamunā, and by such heroic deeds enhance our faith.

s183.v:
(7)
piyato dāvānala rākhobi mo’y
`gopāla’, `govinda’ nāma tava hoy

s183.t: 7) You will surely protect me by swallowing the forest fire. Thus You are called Gopāla (protector of the cows) and Govinda (pleaser of the cows).
8) In order to curb the malice of Indra, king of the demigods, You will protect me from his torrents of rain, O lifter of the mighty Govardhana Hill!

s183.v:
(9)
catur-ānana korabo jab cori
rakhā korobi mujhe, gokula-hari!

s183.t: 9) When the four-headed Brahmā abducts me along with Your cowherd boyfriends and calves, then also You will surely protect me, O Gokula Hari!

s183.v:
(10)
bhakativinoda—tuwā gokula-dhan
rākhobi keśava! korato jatan

s183.t: 10) Bhaktivinoda is now the property of Gokula, Your holy abode. O Keśava! Kindly protect him with gentle loving care.

s184.v:
(1)
choḍato puruṣa-abhimān
kiṅkorī hoiluṅ āji, kān!

s184.t: 1) I give up the vanity of the error that I am a male. Today I have become Your faithful maidservant, O Kāna!
2) In the groves of Vraja I will render personal service as a follower of one of the confidential sakhīs, O Lord of Rādhā!
3) I will string together a garland of forest flowers, in which tulasī buds shall be the jewelled pendants.

s184.v:
(4)
jatane deobuṅ sakhī-kare
hāte laobo sakhī ādare

s184.t: 4) With utmost care I will place the garland in the hands of my superior sakhī, and she will take it out of my hands with loving regard.

s184.v:
(5)
sakhī dibo tuwā duhuk gale
dūrato herobuṅ kutūhale

s184.t: 5) Then she will place the garland around both of Your necks, while from afar I watch in wonder.

s184.v:
(6)
sakhī kahabo,—“śuno sundarī!
rahobi kuñje mama kiṅkorī

s184.t: 6) The confidante will then say to me, “Listen, O beautiful one, you shall remain in this grove as my attendant.
7) “Daily you will string together beautiful flower garlands that will enchant Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

s184.v:
(8)
tuwā rakhana-bhāra hāmārā
mama kuñja-kuṭīra tohārā

s184.t: 8) “The responsibility for your maintenance is mine. My cottage in this grove is yours.
9) “When the time comes for me to go and serve Rādhā and Mādhava, you will stay close to me while remaining hidden.

s184.v:
(10)
tāmbula sāji’ karpūra āni’
deobi moe āpana jāni’ ”

s184.t: 10) “After dressing packets of betel nuts and fetching the camphor, you will hand them to me, knowing me to be your very own.”

s184.v:
(11)
bhakativinoda śuni’ bāt
sakhī-pade kare pranipāt

s184.t: 11) Bhaktivinoda, having heard all these instructions, bows down at the lotus feet of that confidential sakhī.

s185.v:
(1)
tuwā-bhakti-pratikūla dharma jā’te roy
parama jatane tāhā tyajibo niścoy

s185.t: 1) I will assuredly abandon with utmost endeavor all things in which aversion to Your devotional service is inherent.

s185.v:
(2)
tuwā-bhakti-bahir-mukha saṅga nā koribo
gaurāṅga-virodhi-jana-mukha nā heribo

s185.t: 2) I will not keep company with those opposed to Your devotional service, nor even look at the faces of those inimical toward Lord Gaurāṅga.

s185.v:
(3)
bhakti-pratikūla sthāne nā kori vasati
bhaktira apriya kārye nāhi kori rati

s185.t: 3) I will never reside at a place unfavorable for devotional practices, and I will never take pleasure in non-devotional activities.

s185.v:
(4)
bhaktira virodhī grantha pāṭha nā koribo
bhaktira virodhī vyākhyā kabhu nā śunibo

s185.t: 4) I will read no book opposed to pure devotion, nor listen to any scriptural explanation which counters pure devotional principles.

s185.v:
(5)
gaurāṅga-varjita sthāna tīrtha nāhi māni
bhaktira bādhaka jñāna-karma tuccha jāni

s185.t: 5) I will never regard as sacred any place where Lord Gaurāṅga is rejected. All knowledge or action hindering pure devotional service I consider worthless.

s185.v:
(6)
bhaktira bādhaka kāle nā kori ādar
bhakti bahir-mukha nija-jane jāni par

s185.t: 6) Any seasonal observance which poses obstacles to the execution of devotional service finds no favor with me, and I consider as strangers all my own relatives or family members who are averse to devotional service.

s185.v:
(7)
bhaktira bādhikā spṛhā koribo varjan
abhakta-pradatta anna nā kori grahan

s185.t: 7) I will totally abandon all desires that hinder devotion, and I will never touch foodstuffs offered to me by non-devotees.

s185.v:
(8)
jāhā kichu bhakti-pratikūla boli’ jāni
tyajibo jatane tāhā, e niścoya vānī

s185.t: 8) I vow to carefully avoid whatever I know to be contrary to devotional service. This is a most definite proclamation.

s185.v:
(9)
bhakativinoda poḍi’ prabhura caraṇe
māgaye śakati pratikūlyera varjane

s185.t: 9) Bhaktivinoda falls down at the feet of the Lord and begs for the strength to give up all things that are unfavorable to pure devotion.

s186.v:
(1)
viṣaya-vimūḍha ār māyāvādī jan
bhakti-śūnya duṅhe prāna dhare akāraṇ

s186.t: 1) One who is intoxicated by worldly affairs of sense gratification, as well as one who subscribes to impersonal philosophy, both maintain their lives uselessly, for they are devoid of devotion to You.

s186.v:
(2)
ei dui-saṅga nātha! nā hoy āmār
prārthanā koriye āmi caraṇe tomār

s186.t: 2) I pray at Your lotus feet, O Lord, that I may be spared the company of these two kinds of people.

s186.v:
(3)
se duwera madhye viṣayī tabu bhālo
māyāvādī-saṅga nāhi māgi kono kālo

s186.t: 3) Yet of the two, the association of a worldly man is better. I never covet the company of a māyāvādī.

s186.v:
(4)
viṣayī-hṛdoya jabe sādhu-saṅga pāy
anāyāse labhe bhakti bhaktera kṛpāy

s186.t: 4) When by chance the hearts of worldly persons come into contact with Your saintly devotees, they easily attain devotion by the mercy of the devotees.

s186.v:
(5)
māyāvāda-doṣa jā’ra hṛdoye paśilo
kutarke hṛdoya tā’ra vajra-sama bhelo

s186.t: 5) But the heart which is penetrated by the offensive influence of impersonal philosophy becomes hard as a thunderbolt by degraded sophistry.

s186.v:
(6)
bhaktira swarūpa, āra `viṣaya’, `āśroy’
māyāvādī `anitya’ boliyā saba koy

s186.t: 6) The māyāvādī declares that the true form of bhakti, its object (Śrī Kṛṣṇa), and its possessor (the devotee) are all transitory and thus illusory.

s186.v:
(7)
dhik tā’ra kṛṣṇa-sevā-śravana-kīrtan
kṛṣṇa-aṅge vajra hāne tāhāra stavan

s186.t: 7) Fie on his pretense of so-called service to Kṛṣṇa! Fie on his pretense of engaging in so-called hearing and chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s glories! His recitation of prayers strikes the body of Kṛṣṇa with blows more cruel than thunderbolts.

s186.v:
(8)
māyāvāda sama bhakti-pratikūla nāi
ataeva māyāvādī-saṅga nāhi cāi

s186.t: 8) There is no philosophy in the world as antagonistic to devotional service as the impersonal māyāvāda philosophy. Therefore I do not ever desire the association of the māyāvādī.

s186.v:
(9)
bhakativinoda māyāvāda dūra kori
vaiṣṇava-saṅgete baise nāmāśraya dhori’

s186.t: 9) Bhaktivinoda drives away the philosophy of impersonalism and sits safely in the society of Vaiṣṇavas under the shelter of Your holy name.

s187.t: 1) Oh I am a resident of Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja, and a maidservant of the lotus feet of Rādhikā and Mādhava.

s187.v:
(2)
duṅhāra milane ānanda kori
duṅhāra viyoge duḥkhete mari

s187.t: 2) I happily rejoice at the union of the Divine Couple, and in Their separation I die in utter anguish.

s187.v:
(3)
sakhī-sthalī nāhi heri nayane
dekhile śaibyāke paraye mane

s187.t: 3) I never look at the area in Vraja called Sakhī-sthalī where Candrāvalī and her friends live. If I were to see that place it reminds me of Candrāvalī’s sharp-tongued gopī friend named Śaibyā.

s187.v:
(4)
je-je pratikūla candrāra sakhī
prāne duḥkha pāi tāhāre dekhi’

s187.t: 4) I feel pain in my heart whenever I happen to catch sight of Candrāvalī’s proud girlfriends, for they are all inimical to Rādhā’s camp.

s187.v:
(5)
rādhikā-kuñja āṅdhāra kori’
loite cāhe se rādhāra hari

s187.t: 5) Candrāvalī wants to take away Rādhā’s Lord Hari, thus causing the love-grove of Rādhikā to be overcast with the darkness of gloom.
6) I never look at the faces of those who wish to obstruct the joy of the union of Śrī Rādhā and Govinda.

s187.v:
(7)
rādhā-pratikūla jateka jana-
sambhāṣane kabhu nā hoy mana

s187.t: 7) Nor do I find any pleasure in conversing with those who are members of a camp opposed to Rādhā.

s187.v:
(8)
bhakativinoda śrī-rādhā-caraṇe
saṅpeche parāna atīva jatane

s187.t: 8) Bhaktivinoda has entrusted his soul with great care unto the lotus feet of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

s188.v:
(1)
tuwā-bhakti-anukūla je-je kārya hoy
parama-jatane tāhā koribo niścoy

s188.t: 1) I will surely execute with utmost care those activities favorable to Your pure devotional service.

s188.v:
(2)
bhakti-anukūla jata viṣaya saṁsāre
koribo tāhāte rati indriyera dwāre

s188.t: 2) I will feel fondness for those things in this world which are conducive to pure devotion, and with my senses I will engage them in Your service.

s188.v:
(3)
śunibo tomāra kathā jatana koriyā
dekhibo tomāra dhāma nayana bhoriyā

s188.t: 3) I will carefully listen to all discussions concerning You, and the satisfaction of my eyes will be to behold Your divine abode.

s188.v:
(4)
tomāra prasāde deho koribo poṣan
naivedya-tulasī-ghrāna koribo grahan

s188.t: 4) I will nourish my body with the sacred remnants of Your food, and I will smell the sweet scent of tulasī leaves adorning those offerings.

s188.v:
(5)
kara-dwāre koribo tomāra sevā sadā
tomāra vasati-sthale basibo sarvadā

s188.t: 5) With my hands I will always execute Your service, and I will forever dwell at that place where You abide.

s188.v:
(6)
tomāra sevāya kāma niyoga koribo
tomāra vidveṣi-jane krodha dekhāibo

s188.t: 6) I will employ my desires in Your devotional service, and will show my anger to those who are envious of You.

s188.v:
(7)
ei-rūpe sarva-vṛtti āra sarva-bhāva
tuwā anukūla hoye labhuka prabhāva

s188.t: 7) In this way, may all of my propensities and emotions earn spiritual potency by being favorably dovetailed in Your interest.

s188.v:
(8)
tuwā bhakta-anukūla jāhā jāhā kori
tuwā bhakti-anukūla boli’ tāhā dhori

s188.t: 8) Anything I do which gives pleasure to Your devotee I will embrace as conducive to Your devotional service.

s188.v:
(9)
bhakativinoda nāhi jāne dharmādharma
bhakti-anukūla tāra hau saba karma

s188.t: 9) Bhaktivinoda knows neither religion nor irreligion. He simply prays that all his activities be favorable for pure devotion unto You.

s189.t: 1) In the land of Godruma in Navadvīpa, which is very conducive for performing devotional worship of the Supreme Lord, and which is non-different from the sacred place in Vraja called Nandagrām in the holy district of Mathurā…

s189.v:
(2)
tahi māha surabhi-kuñja-kuṭīre
baiṭhobuṅ hāma sura-taṭinī-tīre

s189.t: 2) …There I will settle down in a small cottage within the grove called Surabhi-kuñja on the bank of the celestial Gaṅgā river.
3) I will put on the garb that is dear to the devotees of Lord Gaura-sundara, including the twelve Vaiṣṇava tilaka markings on my body and beautiful beads of tulasī wood around my neck.

s189.v:
(4)
campaka, bakula, kadamba, tamāl
ropato niramibo kuñja viśāl

s189.t: 4) Then, by planting flowering trees like campaka, bakula, kadamba, and tamāl, I will cultivate an extensive grove by my cottage.

s189.v:
(5)
mādhavī mālatī uṭhābuṅ tāhe
chāyā-manḍapa korobuṅ taṅhi māhe

s189.t: 5) I will drape mādhavī and mālatī jasmine creepers upon the trees, and in this way make a shady bower in their midst.

s189.v:
(6)
ropobuṅ tatra kusuma-vana-rāji
jūthi, jāti, mallī virājabo sāji’

s189.t: 6) I will plant row upon row of various forest flowers, including different kinds of jasmine like yuthī, jāti, and mallī. All these will be present there, arrayed in a charming fashion.

s189.v:
(7)
mañce basāobuṅ tulasī-mahārāṇī
kīrtana-sajja taṅhi rākhabo āni’

s189.t: 7) I will install the empress tulasī on an elevated platform in this garden, then procure all necessary paraphernalia for having kīrtana, such as mṛdaṅga drums, karatālas, and gongs, and place them there.

s189.v:
(8)
vaiṣṇava-jana-saha gāobuṅ nām
jaya godruma jaya gaura ki dhām

s189.t: 8) Then I will commence singing the holy names of the Lord in the company of the Vaiṣṇavas. We will sing, “All glories to the island of Godruma! All glories to the divine abode of Lord Gauracandra!”

s189.v:
(9)
bhakativinoda bhakti-anukūl
jaya kuñja, muñja, sura-nadī-kūl

s189.t: 9) Bhaktivinoda is favorably disposed to pure devotional service. All glories to Surabhi-kuñja, to its tall reeds, and to the banks of the celestial Gaṅgā!

s190.v:
(1)
hari he!
arthera sañcaye, viṣaya-prayāse,
āno-kathā-prajalpane
āno-adhikāra, niyama āgrahe,
asat-saṅga-saṁghaṭane

s190.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! I have become absorbed in accumulating wealth and endeavoring for material possessions. I am addicted to idle conversations on topics apart from You. I mistakenly accept duties apart from my own qualifications, and am always eager to adhere to the letter of the law. This is the consequence of associating with worldly men.

s190.v:
(2)
asthira siddhānte, rohinu mojiyā,
hari-bhakti roilo dūre
e hṛdoye mātro, para-hiṁsā, mada,
pratiṣṭhā, śaṭhatā sphure

s190.t: 2) I remain deeply absorbed in the quicksand of ever-changing, uncertain opinions. Therefore, devotion to You has remained distant from me. In this heart of mine dwells only envy and malice towards others, false pride, the desire for fame and honor, and deceitfulness.

s190.v:
(3)
e saba āgraha, chāḍite nārinu,
āpana doṣate mari
janama biphala, hoilo āmāra,
ekhona ki kori, hari!

s190.t: 3) I have not been able to give up any of these inclinations. Thus my own faults have been my downfall. My birth as a human being has been totally wasted. O Lord Hari, what am I to do now?

s190.v:
(4)
āmi to’ patita, patita-pāvana,
tomāra pavitra nāma
se sambandha dhori’, tomāra caraṇe,
śaraṇa loinu hāma

s190.t: 4) I am indeed fallen (patita); but Your pure holy name is Patita-pāvana—the savior of the fallen. Clinging to our relationship as implied by that holy name, I have taken shelter of Your lotus feet.

s191.v:
(1)
hari he!
bhajane utsāha, bhaktite viśvāsa,
prema-labhe dhairya-dhana
bhakti-anukūla, karma-pravartana,
asat-saṅga-visarjana

s191.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Enthusiasm in devotional service, faith in the process of devotional service, the treasure of patience in the attainment of love of God, performing activities favorable to pure devotion, abandoning the company of worldly people…

s191.v:
(2)
bhakti-sadācāra, ei chaya guna,
nāhilo āmāra nātha!
kemone bhojibo, tomāra caraṇa,
chāḍiyā māyāra sātha

s191.t: 2) …performing approved devotional practices—I have never possessed these six devotional qualities, O Lord. How, then, shall I give up my affinity for Māyā and worship Your lotus feet?

s191.v:
(3)
garhita ācāre, rohilāma moji’,
nā korinu sādhu-saṅga
lo’ye sādhu-veśa, āne upadeśi,
e boḍo māyāra raṅga

s191.t: 3) Remaining absorbed in abominable activities, I never kept company with sādhus. Now I adopt the garb of a sādhu and act out the role of instructing others. This is Māyā’s big joke.

s191.v:
(4)
e heno daśāya, ahaitukī kṛpā,
tomāra pāibo, hari!
śrī-guru-āśroye, ḍākibo tomāya,
kabe vā minati kori’

s191.t: 4) O Lord Hari, in such a helpless condition surely I will receive Your causeless mercy. O when, under the shelter of my spiritual master, will I call out to You with my humble entreaty?

s192.v:
(1)
hari he!
dāna, pratigraha, mitho gupta-kathā,
bhakṣana, bhojana-dāna
saṅgera lakṣana, ei chaya hoya,
ihāte bhaktira prāna

s192.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Offering and receiving gifts, giving and receiving spiritual food, revealing one’s thoughts, and making confidential inquiries—these are the six characteristics of loving association, and in them is found the very life of devotion.

s192.v:
(2)
tattva nā bujhiye, jñāne vā ajñāne,
asate e saba kori’
bhakti hārāinu, saṁsārī hoinu,
sudūre rohile hari

s192.t: 2) I have failed to understand the truth, and by practicing these six activities with non-devotees, either knowingly or unknowingly, I lost all devotional inclination and have become a materialist. Consequently You, O Lord, still remain far away.

s192.v:
(3)
kṛṣṇa-bhakta-jane, ei saṅga-lakṣane,
ādara koribo jabe
bhakti-mahā-devī, āmāra hṛdoya-
āsane bosibe tabe

s192.t: 3) The day I cherish these activities of intimate association with the devotees of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, that very day the high goddess of devotion will take her seat upon the throne of my heart.

s192.v:
(4)
yoṣit-saṅgī-jana, kṛṣṇaābhakta āra,
duṅhu-saṅga-parihari’
tava bhakta-jana- saṅga anukṣana,
kabe vā hoibe hari!

s192.t: 4) When will I give up the company of those who are addicted to the company of materialistic women and those who are averse to You? And when will I cultivate the constant association of Your devotees, O Lord?

s193.v:
(1)
hari he!
saṅga-doṣa-śūnya, dīkṣitādīkṣita,
jadi tava nāma gā’ya
mānase ādara, koribo tāhāre,
jāni’ nija-jana tāya

s193.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Within my mind I will honor and consider as my own relative one who naturally avoids the offense of bad association and sings Your holy name, be he formally initiated or not.

s193.v:
(2)
dīkṣita hoiyā, bhaje tuwā pada,
tāhāre pranati kori
ananya-bhajane, vijña yei jana,
tāhāre sevibo, hari!

s193.t: 2) I offer obeisances to that devotee who is initiated and worships Your lotus feet, and I will faithfully serve, O Hari, a devotee who is fixed in unalloyed devotion to You.

s193.v:
(3)
sarva-bhūte sama, ye bhaktera mati,
tāhāra darśane māni
āpanāke dhanya, se saṅga pāiyā,
caritārtha hoiluṅ jāni

s193.t: 3) I consider myself greatly fortunate to even see that devotee who regards all living beings equally. Obtaining his association I consider myself fortunate, for I know that I have become successful in life.

s193.v:
(4)
niṣkapaṭa-mati, vaiṣṇavera prati,
ei dharma kabe pā’bo
kabe saṁsāra- sindhu-pāra ho’ye,
tava braja-pure jā’bo

s193.t: 4) When will my attitude toward the Vaiṣṇavas become simple and innocent? And when will I cross over this ocean of worldly existence and reach Your transcendental abode of Vraja?

s194.v:
(1)
hari he!
nīra-dharma-gata, jāhnavī-salile,
paṅka-phena dṛṣṭa hoya
tathāpi kakhona, brahma-drava-dharma,
se salila nā chāḍoya

s194.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Mud and foam are seen in the waters of the Gaṅgā, for that is the inherent nature of river water. Yet the water of the sacred Gaṅgā never loses its purely spiritual nature.

s194.v:
(2)
vaiṣṇava-śarīra, aprākṛta sadā,
swabhāva-vapura dharme
kabhu nāhe jaḍa, tathāpi ye ninde,
poḍe se viṣamādharme

s194.t: 2) One may likewise find natural defects in the body of a Vaiṣṇava, yet his body is always spiritual. It is never to be considered material. That person who criticizes the body of a Vaiṣṇava falls into deadly irreligion.

s194.v:
(3)
sei aparādhe, yamera jātanā,
pāya jīva avirata
he nanda-nandana! sei aparādhe,
yeno nāhi hoi hata

s194.t: 3) For such an offense, the fallen soul ceaselessly suffers the tortures of Yamarāja, lord of death. O youthful son of Nanda! I pray that I will not be destroyed by committing such an offense.

s194.v:
(4)
tomāra vaiṣṇava, vaibhava tomāra,
āmāre korunā doyā
tabe mora gati, ha’be tava prati,
pā’bo tava pada-chāyā

s194.t: 4) The Vaiṣṇava is Your own, representing Your glorious divine potency. May he be merciful to me. Then my life’s journey will turn toward You, and I will attain shelter in the shade of Your lotus feet.

s195.v:
(1)
hari he!
tomāre bhuliyā, avidyā-pīḍāya,
pīḍita rasanā mora
kṛṣṇa-nāma-sudhā, bhālo nāhi lāge,
viṣaya-sukhate bhora

s195.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Because of forgetting You, my tongue has become embittered with the disease of ignorance. I cannot relish the sweet nectar of Your holy name of Kṛṣṇa, for I have become addicted to the taste of worldly pleasures.

s195.v:
(2)
prati-dina jadi, ādara koriyā,
se nāma kīrtana kori
sitapala jeno, nāśi’ roga-mūla,
krame swādu hoya, hari!

s195.t: 2) If I sing that holy name of Yours aloud every day with warm affection, then as sugar candy taken medicinally destroys the very disease which makes it taste bitter (jaundice), so Your holy name, O Lord Hari, will cure my spiritual disease and allow me to gradually taste Your sweetness.

s195.v:
(3)
durdaiva āmāra, se nāme ādara,
nā hoilo, doyāmoya!
daśa aparādha, āmāra durdaiva,
kemone hoibe kṣoya

s195.t: 3) How great is my misfortune that I feel no appreciation for Your holy name, O merciful Lord! In such a lamentable state, how will I be freed from committing the ten offenses to the holy name?

s195.v:
(4)
anudina jeno, tava nāma gāi,
kramete kṛpāya tava
aparādha jā’be, nāme ruci ha’be,
āswādibo nāmāsava

s195.t: 4) If I sing Your name every day, then gradually by Your mercy the ten offenses will disappear, taste for Your holy name will grow within me, and then I shall relish the intoxicating wine of that name.

s196.v:
(1)
hari he!
śrī-rūpa-gosāi, śrī-guru-rūpete,
śikṣā dila mora kāne
“jāno mora kathā, nāmera kāṅgāla!
rati pā’be nāma-gāne

s196.t: 1) O my Lord Hari! Śrī Rūpa Goswāmī, in the form of the spiritual master, spoke these instructions into my ears: “Try to understand my words, O you who beg for the gift of the holy name! You will then develop attraction for singing the holy name.

s196.v:
(2)
kṛṣṇa-nāma-rūpa- guna-sucarita,
parama jatane kori’
rasanā-mānase, koraho niyoga,
krama-vidhi anusari’

s196.t: 2) “Following the scriptural rules and regulations, engage your tongue and your mind in carefully cultivating Lord Kṛṣṇa’s nāma (holy names), rūpa (divine forms), guna (transcendental qualities), and sucarita (wonderful pastimes). This should be done according to the recommended order of ascending progression.

s196.v:
(3)
braje kori’ bāsa, rāgānugā hoiyā,
smaraṇa kīrtana koro
e nikhila kāla, koraho jāpana,
upadeśa-sāra dharo’ ”

s196.t: 3) “Always dwelling in the holy land of Vraja, become a practitioner of rāgānugā-bhakti (spontaneous loving devotion) while engaging in smaraṇa (remembrance) and kīrtana (glorification). Spend every moment of your time in these ways. Just accept this as the essence of all instructions.”

s196.v:
(4)
hā! rūpa-gosāi, doyā kori’ kabe,
dibe dine braja-bāsa
rāgātmika tumi, tava padānuga,
hoite dāsera āśā

s196.t: 4) O Rūpa Goswāmī! When will you, out of your causeless mercy, enable this poor wretched soul to reside in Vraja? You are a rāgātmika devotee—an eternally liberated, intimate associate of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. This humble servant of yours desires to become a loyal follower of your lotus feet.

s197.v:
(1)
gurudev!
kabe mora sei din ha’be
mana sthira kori’, nirjane bosiyā,
kṛṣṇa-nāma gā’bo jabe
saṁsāra-phukāra, kāne nā poṣibe,
deho-roga dūre ro’be

s197.t: 1) O Gurudeva! When will that day be mine? With a steady mind, sitting in a secluded place, I will sing the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The tumultuous pandemonium of worldly existence will no longer echo in my ears, and the diseases of the body will remain far away.

s197.v:
(2)
`hare kṛṣṇa’ boli’, gāhite gāhite,
nayane bohibe lora
dehete pulaka, udita hoibe,
premete koribe bhora

s197.t: 2) When I chant “Hare Kṛṣṇa” tears of love will flow and flow from my eyes. Ecstatic rapture will arise within my body, causing my hair to stand on end and my entire being to become overwhelmed with divine love.

s197.v:
(3)
gada-gada vānī, mukhe bāhiribe,
kāṅpibe śarīra mama
gharma muhur muhuḥ, virvarna hoibe,
stambhita pralaya sama

s197.t: 3) Faltering words choked with emotion will issue from my mouth. My body will tremble, constantly perspire, turn pale and discolored, and become stunned. All of this will be like a devastation of ecstatic love and cause me to fall unconscious.

s197.v:
(4)
niṣkapaṭe heno, daśā kabe ha’be,
nirantara nāma gā’bo
āveśe rohiyā, deha-yātrā kori’,
tomāra karunā pā’bo

s197.t: 4) When will such a genuine ecstatic condition be mine? I will constantly sing the holy name and remain absorbed in profound devotion while traveling in the material body. In this way I will receive your mercy.

s198.v:
(1)
gurudev!
kabe tava karunā-prakāśe
śrī-gaurāṅga-līlā, hoya nitya-tattwa,
ei dṛḍha viśvāse
`hari hari’ boli’, godruma-kānane,
bhromibo darśana-āśe

s198.t: 1) O Gurudeva! When will it be, as a manifestation of your mercy? I will become fixed in the firm faith that Lord Gaurāṅga’s pastimes are eternal realities. Chanting “Hari! Hari!” I will wander throughout the groves of Godruma, hoping to catch a glimpse of those pastimes.

s198.v:
(2)
nitāi, gaurāṅga, adwaita, śrīvāsa,
gadādhara,—pañca-jana
kṛṣṇa-nāma-rase, bhāsā’be jagat,
kori’ mahā-saṅkīrtana

s198.t: 2) The five personalities—Nitāi, Gaurāṅga, Advaita, Śrīvāsa, and Gadādhara—will flood the entire universe with the intoxicating nectar of the holy name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa by performing a mahā-saṅkīrtan.

s198.v:
(3)
nartana-vilāsa, mṛdaṅga-vādana,
śunibo āpana-kāne
dekhiyā dekhiyā, se līlā-mādhurī,
bhāsibo premera bāne

s198.t: 3) With my own ears I will hear the sounds of playful dancing and the rhythmic pulsations of the mṛdaṅga drums. By constantly looking and looking upon the sweetness and beauty of that pastime, I will float in the floodtide of divine love.

s198.v:
(4)
nā dekhi’ ābāra, se līlā-ratana,
kāṅdi hā gaurāṅga! boli’
āmāre viṣayī, pāgala boliyā,
aṅgete dibeka dhūli

s198.t: 4) The next moment losing sight of the jewel of that pastime, I shall weep and cry out, “O my Lord Gaurāṅga!” Materialists will then proclaim me thoroughly mad and will throw dust upon my body.

s199.v:
(1)
dekhite dekhite, bhulibo vā kabe,
nija-sthūla-paricoya
nayane heribo, braja-pura-śobhā,
nitya cid-ānanda-moya

s199.t: 1) When, in a flash, will I forget my gross bodily indentity? I will behold the exquisite beauty of the realm of Vraja, full of eternal spiritual bliss.

s199.v:
(2)
bṛṣabhānu-pure, janama loibo,
yāvaṭe vivāha ha’be
braja-gopī-bhāva, hoibe swabhāva,
āno-bhāva nā rohibe

s199.t: 2) I shall have my birth in the town of King Vṛṣabhānu, and eventually be married nearby in Yāvaṭ-grām. My sole disposition and character shall be that of a cowherd girl, and I shall know no other mood.

s199.v:
(3)
nija-siddha-deha, nija-siddha-nāma,
nija-rūpa-swa-vasana
rādhā-kṛpā-bale, lobhibo vā kabe,
kṛṣṇa-prema-prakaraṇa

s199.t: 3) When will I obtain, by the power of Rādhā’s mercy, my own eternal spiritual body, my own realized name, my own form, and my own dress? And when, by Her mercy, will I receive initiation into the techniques of expressing divine love for Kṛṣṇa?

s199.v:
(4)
jamunā-salila- āharaṇe giyā,
bujhibo yugala-rasa
prema-mugdha ho’ye, pāgalinī-prāya,
gāibo rādhāra yaśa

s199.t: 4) As I go to draw water from the Yamunā, I shall cherish knowing the confidential mellows that unite the divine pair Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Being enchanted by sublime love, I will sing Śrī Rādhā’s glories just like a madwoman.

s200.v:
(1)
bṛṣabhānu-sutā- caraṇa-sevane,
hoibo ye pālya-dāsī
śrī-rādhāra sukha, satata sādhane,
rohibo āmi prayāsī

s200.t: 1) For serving the lotus feet of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, I shall become a protected maidservant of one of the gopīs in Vraja. I will always strive to bring about the pleasure of Śrī Rādhā.

s200.v:
(2)
śrī-rādhāra sukhe, kṛṣṇaera ye sukha,
jānibo manete āmi
rādhā-pada chāḍi’, śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅgame,
kabhu nā hoibo kāmī

s200.t: 2) Within my heart I will know that Rādhā’s pleasure is Kṛṣṇa’s only source of joy. Therefore, I will never desire to abandon Her lotus feet for enjoying His exclusive company.

s200.v:
(3)
sakhī-gaṇa mama, parama-suhṛt,
yugala-premera guru
tad-anugā ho’ye, sevibo rādhāra,
caraṇa-kalapa-taru

s200.t: 3) The sakhīs are my best friends and teachers concerning the love uniting Rādhā with Kṛṣṇa. By following their example, I shall serve Rādhā’s lotus feet, which are like wish-fulfilling trees.

s200.v:
(4)
rādhā-pakṣa chāḍi’, ye-jana se-jana,
ye bhāve se bhāve thāke
āmi to’ rādhikā- pakṣa-pātī sadā,
kabhu nāhi heri tā’ke

s200.t: 4) I myself am always partial to Rādhikā’s camp and therefore never look upon those who have abandoned Rādhā’s entourage, whoever they may be and whatever their ways.

s201.v:
(1)
kṛṣṇa-nāma dhare koto bal
viṣaya-vāsanānale, mora citta sadā jwale,
ravi-tapta maru-bhūmi-sam
karna-randhra-patha diyā, hṛdi mājhe praveśiyā,
variṣoya sudhā anupam

s201.t: 1) What power does the name of Kṛṣṇa possess? My heart constantly burns in the fire of worldly desires, just like a desert scorched by the rays of the sun. The holy name, entering the core of my heart through the holes of my ears, showers unparalleled nectar upon my soul.

s201.v:
(2)
hṛdoya hoite bole, jihvāra agrete cale,
śabda-rūpe nāce anukṣan
kanṭhe mora bhaṅge swara, aṅga kāṅpe thara thara,
sthira hoite nā pāre caraṇ

s201.t: 2) The holy name speaks from within my heart, moves onto the tip of my tongue, and constantly dances on it in the form of transcendental sound. My throat becomes choked up, my body shivers again and again, and my feet cannot remain still.

s201.v:
(3)
cakṣe dhārā, dehe gharma, pulakita saba carma,
vivarna hoilo kalevara
mūrchita hoilo man, pralayera āgaman,
bhāve sarva-deha jara jara

s201.t: 3) Rivers of tears flow from my eyes, perspiration completely soaks my body, all my skin thrills with rapture, my hairs stand on end, and my complexion turns pale and discolored. My mind grows faint, I begin to experience devastation, and my entire body is shattered in a flood of ecstatic emotions.

s201.v:
(4)
kori’ eto upadrava, citte varṣe sudhā-drava,
more ḍāre premera sāgare
kichu nā bujhite dilo, more to’ bātula koilo,
mora citta-vitta saba hare

s201.t: 4) While causing such an ecstatic disturbance, the holy name showers liquid nectar on my heart and drowns me in the ocean of divine love of Godhead. He does not allow me to understand anything, for He has made me truly mad by having stolen away my mind and all my resources.

s201.v:
(5)
loinu āśroya jā’r, heno vyavahāra tā’r,
varnite nā pāri e sakal
kṛṣṇa-nāma icchā-moy, jāhe jāhe sukhī hoy,
sei mora sukhera sambal

s201.t: 5) Such is the behavior of Him in whom I have taken shelter. I am not capable of describing all this. The holy name of Kṛṣṇa is independent and thus acts on His own sweet will. In whatever way He becomes happy, that is also my way of happiness.

s201.v:
(6)
premera kalikā nām, adbhuta rasera dhām,
heno bala karaye prakāś
īṣat vikaśi’ punaḥ, dekhāy nija-rūpa-guna,
citta hari’ loya kṛṣṇa-pāś

s201.t: 6) The holy name is the bud of the flower of divine love, and is the very abode of astonishing mellows. Such is the power He manifests that when His holy name starts to blossom a little further, it then reveals His own divine form and qualities. Thus my heart is abducted and taken directly to Kṛṣṇa.

s201.v:
(7)
pūrna vikaśita hoiyā, braje more jāya loiyā,
dekhāy more swarūpa-vilās
more siddha-deha diyā, kṛṣṇa-pāśe rākhe giyā,
e dehera kore sarva-nāś

s201.t: 7) Blossoming fully, the flower of the holy name takes me to Vraja and reveals to me His own love-dalliance. This name gives to me my own eternal spiritual body, keeps me right by Kṛṣṇa’s side, and completely destroys everything related to this mortal frame of mine.

s201.v:
(8)
kṛṣṇa-nāma-cintāmaṇi, akhila rasera khani,
nitya-mukta śuddha-rasa-moy
nāmera bālāi jata, saba lo’ye hoi hata,
tabe mora sukhera udoy

s201.t: 8) The name of Kṛṣṇa is a transcendental touchstone, a mine of all devotional mellows. It is eternally liberated, and the embodiment of pure rasa. When all impediments to the pure chanting of the holy name are taken away and destroyed, then my happiness will know its true awakening.
